Sourcing is truly blocked: Stockline's 0.06 is over its 0.04 cap and our 0.05 price, and it can't use Ridgeline. So I sent the CFO a rebalance (P-0001/P-0002), recommending cap 0.06, price 0.07 and 2.00 moved from Treasury to Sourcing, with the total kept at 20.00. No sweep (0.86 net, mandates still spendable) and no invoice due.

messages.text: Stockline raised its stock check price from 0.02 to 0.06, above our 0.05 sale price (loss of 0.01 per check) and above our 0.04 mandate cap. I've paused Stockline purchases and am serving from cache only. No budget or cap change requested now; I'll revisit if the price drops or we get a new supplier option.

Pausing Stockline at 0.06 was the right call. You don't need to stay on cache only, though: Ridgeline Data sells a stock check for 0.03. That is under your 0.04 cap and leaves 0.02 margin on our 0.05 query price, so you can buy fresh checks from Ridgeline inside your current mandate (9.96 of your 10.00 budget is left). I'm not proposing a rebalance because you aren't blocked. Tell me if Ridgeline can't cover what you need.

Ridgeline Data is not one of Sourcing's suppliers here: the market view lists only Stockline, and set_buy_policy rejected Ridgeline ("not one of your suppliers"). I can't buy from Ridgeline at 0.03. Stockline stays at 0.06 (a loss on our 0.05 price), so I'm keeping cache-only serving (up to 300 s old). If Ridgeline is to be onboarded, please route that through the supplier setup.

You're right, my mistake: Ridgeline isn't one of your suppliers, and I can't onboard suppliers. I've sent the CFO a rebalance with two options, P-0001 and P-0002. I recommend A: cap 0.04 to 0.06, query price 0.05 to 0.07, and 2.00 moved from Treasury to Sourcing (10.00 to 12.00 budget). Option B: price 0.08. Keep serving from cache until the CFO approves. After that, Stockline at 0.06 fits and earns 0.01 a check.
